claim: SETD3 is a member of the SET (Su(var)3–9, Enhancer of zeste, and Trithorax) domain protein superfamily.
source: SETD3 is a member of the SET (Su(var)3–9, Enhancer of zeste, and Trithorax) domain protein superfamily and plays important roles in hypoxic pulmonary hypertension, muscle differentiation, and carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a classification of SETD3.

claim: SETD3 plays important roles in hypoxic pulmonary hypertension, muscle differentiation, and carcinogenesis.
source: SETD3 is a member of the SET (Su(var)3–9, Enhancer of zeste, and Trithorax) domain protein superfamily and plays important roles in hypoxic pulmonary hypertension, muscle differentiation, and carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as known functions of SETD3.

claim: SETD3 was previously identified as the actin-specific methyltransferase that methylates the N3 of His73 on β-actin.
source: Previously, we identified SETD3 as the actin-specific methyltransferase that methylates the N3 of His73 on β-actin (Kwiatkowski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract with a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Two structures of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine-bound SETD3 in complex with either an unmodified β-actin peptide or its His-methylated variant were determined.
source: Here, we present two structures of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine-bound SETD3 in complex with either an unmodified β-actin peptide or its His-methylated variant.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: The recognition and methylation of β-actin by SETD3 are highly sequence specific.
source: Structural analyses, supported by biochemical experiments and enzyme activity assays, indicate that the recognition and methylation of β-actin by SETD3 are highly sequence specific, and that both SETD3 and β-actin adopt pronounced conformational changes upon binding to each other.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from structural analyses, biochemical experiments, and enzyme activity assays.

claim: Both SETD3 and β-actin adopt pronounced conformational changes upon binding to each other.
source: Structural analyses, supported by biochemical experiments and enzyme activity assays, indicate that the recognition and methylation of β-actin by SETD3 are highly sequence specific, and that both SETD3 and β-actin adopt pronounced conformational changes upon binding to each other.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from structural analyses.

claim: This study is the first to show a catalytic mechanism of SETD3-mediated histidine methylation on β-actin.
source: In conclusion, this study is the first to show a catalytic mechanism of SETD3-mediated histidine methylation on β-actin, which not only throws light on the protein histidine methylation phenomenon but also facilitates the design of small molecule inhibitors of SETD3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion of the study.

claim: There are six actin isoforms in mammalian cells characterized on the basis of their different expression profiles and cellular functions.
source: There are six actin isoforms in mammalian cells that are characterized on the basis of their different expression profiles and cellular functions, including αskeletal-, αcardiac-, αsmooth-, βcyto-, γcyto-, and γsmooth-actins (Gunning et al., 1983; Herman, 1993; Perrin and Ervasti, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: β-actin is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in cytoskeleton formation, cell motility and maintenance of cell stability.
source: Among these, β-actin is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in a wide variety of cellular functions, such as cytoskeleton formation, cell motility and maintenance of cell stability (Leterrier et al., 2017; Nudel et al., 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: N3-methylation of His73 in β-actin was identified in 1967.
source: N3-methylation of His73 in β-actin has been of special interest since its identification in 1967 (Johnson et al., 1967), not only because of the extreme evolutionary conservation of this PTM–methylated His, which is present in almost all eukaryotic actins, but mainly because the methylation of H73 decreases the hydrolysis rate of the actin-bound ATP (Kabsch et al., 1990), as evidenced by the greater ATP exchange rate in the actin-H73A mutant (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Johnson et al., 1967.

claim: Methylated His73 is present in almost all eukaryotic actins.
source: N3-methylation of His73 in β-actin has been of special interest since its identification in 1967 (Johnson et al., 1967), not only because of the extreme evolutionary conservation of this PTM–methylated His, which is present in almost all eukaryotic actins, but mainly because the methylation of H73 decreases the hydrolysis rate of the actin-bound ATP (Kabsch et al., 1990), as evidenced by the greater ATP exchange rate in the actin-H73A mutant (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a characteristic of the methylation.

claim: The methylation of H73 decreases the hydrolysis rate of the actin-bound ATP.
source: N3-methylation of His73 in β-actin has been of special interest since its identification in 1967 (Johnson et al., 1967), not only because of the extreme evolutionary conservation of this PTM–methylated His, which is present in almost all eukaryotic actins, but mainly because the methylation of H73 decreases the hydrolysis rate of the actin-bound ATP (Kabsch et al., 1990), as evidenced by the greater ATP exchange rate in the actin-H73A mutant (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Kabsch et al., 1990 and Nyman et al., 2002.

claim: The actin-H73A mutant has a greater ATP exchange rate.
source: N3-methylation of His73 in β-actin has been of special interest since its identification in 1967 (Johnson et al., 1967), not only because of the extreme evolutionary conservation of this PTM–methylated His, which is present in almost all eukaryotic actins, but mainly because the methylation of H73 decreases the hydrolysis rate of the actin-bound ATP (Kabsch et al., 1990), as evidenced by the greater ATP exchange rate in the actin-H73A mutant (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Nyman et al., 2002.

claim: The presence of actin-specific methyltransferases was shown in rabbit muscles decades ago.
source: Although the presence of actin-specific methyltransferases was shown in rabbit muscles decades ago (Raghavan et al., 1992; Vijayasarathy and Rao, 1987), the molecular identity of this enzyme has long been unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Raghavan et al., 1992 and Vijayasarathy and Rao, 1987.

claim: SETD3 was recently identified as the actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase that methylates actin at His73.
source: Recently, we and others identified SETD3 as the actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase that methylates actin at His73 (Kwiatkowski et al., 2018; Wilkinson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Kwiatkowski et al., 2018 and Wilkinson et al., 2019.

claim: The SET domain is a ~130 amino acids motif initially identified in Drosophila proteins.
source: SETD3 is a member of the SET domain family, the SET domain being a ~ 130 amino acids (aa) motif initially identified in Drosophila proteins, with its acronym derived from three histone lysine methyltransferases: Su(var)3–9, Enhancer of zeste, and Trithorax (Dillon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Dillon et al., 2005.

claim: Most known histone lysine methyltransferases contain a SET domain.
source: To date, most known histone lysine methyltransferases contain a SET domain, although there are some exceptions such as DOT1L (Min et al., 2003), METTL12 (Rhein et al., 2017), and METTL21B (Malecki et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to exceptions.

claim: SET domain proteins transfer a methyl moiety from S-adenosyl methionine (AdoMet) to substrates to generate a methylated form of the substrate, with S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (AdoHcy) as the co-product.
source: Before SETD3 was identified as an actin-specific histidine methyltransferase, SET domain proteins were known to act as lysine methyltransferases, transferring a methyl moiety from the methyl donor S-adenosyl methionine (AdoMet) to the substrates to generate a methylated form of the substrate, with S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (AdoHcy) as the co-product (Dillon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Dillon et al., 2005.

claim: SETD3 has been identified previously as a histone methyltransferase that methylates histone H3 at Lys4 and Lys36.
source: As (i) SETD3 has been identified previously as a histone methyltransferase that methylates histone H3 at Lys4 and Lys36 (Eom et al., 2011; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012) and as (ii) the results of our preliminary experiments using isothermal calorimetry titration (ITC) and mass spectrometry had revealed that SETD3 binds to and methylates a β-actin peptide containing His73 (66–88) (but not H3K4 (1–23) or H3K36 (25–47) peptides), we crystallized and solved two structures of AdoHcy-bound SETD3 in complex with either the His73 peptide or the 3-methylhistidine (His73me) peptide to determine the molecular mechanism of SETD3-mediated histidine methylation of β-actin.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Eom et al., 2011 and Wagner and Carpenter, 2012.

claim: SETD3 binds to and methylates a β-actin peptide containing His73 (66–88).
source: As (i) SETD3 has been identified previously as a histone methyltransferase that methylates histone H3 at Lys4 and Lys36 (Eom et al., 2011; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012) and as (ii) the results of our preliminary experiments using isothermal calorimetry titration (ITC) and mass spectrometry had revealed that SETD3 binds to and methylates a β-actin peptide containing His73 (66–88) (but not H3K4 (1–23) or H3K36 (25–47) peptides), we crystallized and solved two structures of AdoHcy-bound SETD3 in complex with either the His73 peptide or the 3-methylhistidine (His73me) peptide to determine the molecular mechanism of SETD3-mediated histidine methylation of β-actin.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a result of preliminary experiments.

claim: SETD3 does not bind to or methylate H3K4 (1–23) or H3K36 (25–47) peptides.
source: As (i) SETD3 has been identified previously as a histone methyltransferase that methylates histone H3 at Lys4 and Lys36 (Eom et al., 2011; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012) and as (ii) the results of our preliminary experiments using isothermal calorimetry titration (ITC) and mass spectrometry had revealed that SETD3 binds to and methylates a β-actin peptide containing His73 (66–88) (but not H3K4 (1–23) or H3K36 (25–47) peptides), we crystallized and solved two structures of AdoHcy-bound SETD3 in complex with either the His73 peptide or the 3-methylhistidine (His73me) peptide to determine the molecular mechanism of SETD3-mediated histidine methylation of β-actin.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a result of preliminary experiments.

claim: SETD3 recognizes a fragment of β-actin in a sequence-dependent manner.
source: Having solved the two peptide-bound structures of SETD3, we reveal that SETD3 recognizes a fragment of β-actin in a sequence-dependent manner and utilizes a specific pocket to catalyze the N3-methylation of His73.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from the structural studies.

claim: SETD3 utilizes a specific pocket to catalyze the N3-methylation of His73.
source: Having solved the two peptide-bound structures of SETD3, we reveal that SETD3 recognizes a fragment of β-actin in a sequence-dependent manner and utilizes a specific pocket to catalyze the N3-methylation of His73.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from the structural studies.

claim: SETD3 core region (aa 2–502) binds to the β-actin peptide (aa 66–88) with a Kd of 0.17 μM.
source: We measured the binding affinity of the SETD3 core region (aa 2–502) to a His73-containing fragment of β-actin (aa 66–88) by ITC and found that SETD3 binds to the β-actin peptide with a Kd of 0.17 μM (Figure 1A–B and Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to ITC data in Figure 1 and Table 1.

claim: Neither H3K4(1–23) nor H3K36(25–47) peptides bind to SETD3.
source: Given that SETD3 has also been reported to be a putative lysine methyltransferase that methylates Lys4 and Lys36 of histone H3 (Eom et al., 2011), we also examined the binding of SETD3 to two different histone peptides, H3K4(1–23) and H3K36(25–47), and found that neither of these peptides binds to SETD3 (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 1.

claim: SETD3 methylates the β-actin peptide (66–88).
source: Furthermore, we detected the activity of SETD3 on β-actin(66–88), H3K4(1–23), and H3K36(25–47) by mass spectrometry and found that SETD3 methylates the β-actin peptide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) but does not modify either H3K4 or H3K36 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to mass spectrometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SETD3 does not modify either H3K4 or H3K36 peptides.
source: Furthermore, we detected the activity of SETD3 on β-actin(66–88), H3K4(1–23), and H3K36(25–47) by mass spectrometry and found that SETD3 methylates the β-actin peptide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) but does not modify either H3K4 or H3K36 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to mass spectrometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–1C.

claim: No methylated product was detected for any of the three peptides in the presence of AdoMet without the addition of SETD3.
source: No methylated product was detected for any of the three peptides in the presence of AdoMet without the addition of SETD3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–1C.

claim: SETD3 did not methylate the β-actin(66–88) H73A mutant.
source: Moreover, SETD3 did not methylate the β-actin(66–88) H73A mutant, although binding of the mutant peptide to SETD3 is only ~2.5 fold weaker than that of the wild-type peptide (0.45 μM vs. 0.17 μM) (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Binding of the β-actin H73A mutant peptide to SETD3 is only ~2.5 fold weaker than that of the wild-type peptide (0.45 μM vs. 0.17 μM).
source: Moreover, SETD3 did not methylate the β-actin(66–88) H73A mutant, although binding of the mutant peptide to SETD3 is only ~2.5 fold weaker than that of the wild-type peptide (0.45 μM vs. 0.17 μM) (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: SETD3 specifically binds to the β-actin peptide and methylates it at His73.
source: Collectively, the binding experiments and mass spectrometry data indicate that SETD3 specifically binds to the β-actin peptide and methylates it at His73.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from binding and mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: A 1.95 Å structure of AdoHcy-bound SETD3(2–502) with β-actin(66–88) was obtained.
source: By using the core region of SETD3(2–502) with the β-actin peptide(66–88), we succeeded in crystallizing the complex and obtained a 1.95 Å structure of AdoHcy-bound SETD3(2–502) with β-actin(66–88) (Table 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 2 and figures.

claim: There are four molecules in a crystallographic asymmetric unit of the AdoHcy-bound SETD3 with β-actin complex.
source: There are four molecules in a crystallographic asymmetric unit and residues 22–501 of SETD3 and 66–84 of β-actin are visible in the complex structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Residues 22–501 of SETD3 and 66–84 of β-actin are visible in the complex structures.
source: There are four molecules in a crystallographic asymmetric unit and residues 22–501 of SETD3 and 66–84 of β-actin are visible in the complex structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: His73 of β-actin had been methylated in the structure, although an unmethylated peptide was used.
source: On the basis of the density map, we found that His73 of β-actin had been methylated in the structure (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A), although we used an unmethylated peptide.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to the density map in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A.

claim: SETD3 bound to the methyl donor AdoMet from Escherichia coli and methylated the peptide at His73 during crystallization.
source: The reason for this could be that SETD3 bound to the methyl donor AdoMet from Escherichia coli, which we used to express our protein, and that the AdoMet-bound SETD3 methylated the peptide at His73 during crystallization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an explanation for the methylation observed in the structure.

claim: The complex of AdoHcy-bound SETD3 with methylated β-actin represents a snapshot of the post-methyl transfer state.
source: Therefore, this complex represents a snapshot of the post- methyl transfer state, which prompted us to crystallize the substrate-bound enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the structure.

claim: A 2.15 Å structure of AdoHcy-bound SETD3 with unmodified β-actin peptide was obtained.
source: The complex was crystallized and solved at a resolution of 2.15 Å (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 2.

claim: There are two molecules in a crystallographic asymmetric unit of the substrate-bound SETD3 complex.
source: There are two molecules in a crystallographic asymmetric unit (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: In the substrate-bound structure, the density map of the peptide indicates that it is unmodified.
source: In this structure, the density map of the peptide indicates that it is unmodified, suggesting that methylation did not occur (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to the density map in Figure 1—figure supplement 5B.

claim: The substrate-bound complex structure reflects the image of the pre-methyl transfer state.
source: The complex structure therefore reflects the image of the pre-methyl transfer state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the structure.

claim: The SETD3 core region adopts a V-shape architecture and is composed of N-SET, SET, iSET, and C-SET domains.
source: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, the SETD3 core region adopts a V-shape architecture and is composed of N-SET (N-terminal to the SET domain), SET, iSET (an insertion in the SET domain), and C-SET (C-terminal to the SET domain) domains (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The N-terminal lobe of SETD3 contains the N-SET, SET, and iSET domains.
source: The N-terminal lobe contains the N-SET (α1–α3), SET (β1–β12), and iSET (α4–α11) domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The N-SET domain consists of three α helices (α1–α3) and encompasses the SET and iSET domains.
source: The N-SET domain consists of three α helices (α1–α3), and encompasses the SET and iSET domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The SET domain adopts a canonical SET domain fold similar to that of LSMT.
source: The SET domain adopts a canonical SET domain fold similar to that of LSMT (Trievel et al., 2002), with twelve β strands arranged into four anti-parallel β sheets (β1-β2, β3-β11, β4-β10-β9, β5-β7-β6) and one parallel β sheet (β8-β12) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to LSMT and figures.

claim: The iSET domain is a helical region (α4–α11) inserted between β5 and β6 of the SET domain.
source: The iSET domain is a helical region (α4–α11) inserted between β5 and β6 of the SET domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The C-terminal lobe consists of just the C-SET domain.
source: The C-terminal lobe, consisting of just the C-SET domain, is almost entirely helical (α12–α19) except for two anti-parallel strands (β13–β14), with α12 and the N-terminal end of α19 packed against α10 and α9 of iSET, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The overall fold of SETD3 is highly similar to those of LSMT (Z-core: 31.4, RMSD: 3.8 Å for 425 Cα atoms) and SETD6 (Z-core: 28.7, RMSD: 2.8 Å for 421 Cα atoms), despite the low sequence identities (24–25%).
source: Consistently, a database search using the DALI server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010) revealed that the overall fold of SETD3 is highly similar to those of LSMT (Z-core: 31.4, RMSD: 3.8 Å for 425 Cα atoms) and SETD6 (Z-core: 28.7, RMSD: 2.8 Å for 421 Cα atoms), despite the low sequence identities (24–25%).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to DALI server analysis.

claim: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, AdoHcy is located at a cleft in SETD3 formed by the SET and C-SETD domains, and is buttressed by iSET at the bottom.
source: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, AdoHcy is located at a cleft in SETD3 formed by the SET and C-SETD domains, and is buttressed by iSET at the bottom (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The adenine ring of AdoHcy is sandwiched between the side chain of Glu104 and the aromatic ring of Phe327, forming stacking and π–π interactions.
source: Specifically, the adenine ring of AdoHcy is sandwiched between the side chain of Glu104 and the aromatic ring of Phe327, forming stacking and π–π interactions with Glu104 and Phe327, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The N6 and N7 atoms of AdoHcy are hydrogen-bonded to the main chain carbonyl and amide groups of His279, respectively.
source: The N6 and N7 atoms of AdoHcy are hydrogen-bonded to the main chain carbonyl and amide groups of His279, respectively, while the AdoHcy C8 atom forms one C-H...O hydrogen bond with the hydroxyl group of Tyr313 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The AdoHcy C8 atom forms one C-H...O hydrogen bond with the hydroxyl group of Tyr313.
source: The N6 and N7 atoms of AdoHcy are hydrogen-bonded to the main chain carbonyl and amide groups of His279, respectively, while the AdoHcy C8 atom forms one C-H...O hydrogen bond with the hydroxyl group of Tyr313 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The ribose O3′ and O4′ atoms of AdoHcy form hydrogen bonds with the main chain carbonyl of Ser325 and the side chain carboxyl of Asn278, respectively.
source: In addition to the adenine-specific interactions, the ribose O3′ and O4′ atoms of AdoHcy form hydrogen bonds with the main chain carbonyl of Ser325 and the side chain carboxyl of Asn278, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The side chain carboxyl of Asn278 makes a hydrogen bond with the AdoHcy amide.
source: The side chain carboxyl of Asn278 makes another hydrogen bond with the AdoHcy amide, and the latter is also H-bonded to the main chain carbonyl of Phe106 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The AdoHcy amide is hydrogen-bonded to the main chain carbonyl of Phe106.
source: The side chain carboxyl of Asn278 makes another hydrogen bond with the AdoHcy amide, and the latter is also H-bonded to the main chain carbonyl of Phe106 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: The AdoHcy carboxylate group forms four hydrogen bonds with SETD3 residues: one with the main chain amide of Phe106, one with the guanidino group of Arg254, and two with the guanidino group of Arg75.
source: The AdoHcy carboxylate group forms four hydrogen bonds with SETD3 residues: one with the main chain amide of Phe106, one with the guanidino group of Arg254, and the other two with the guanidino group of Arg75 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: All AdoHcy-binding residues are conserved in other SETD3 orthologs, suggesting a conserved function of SETD3.
source: All AdoHcy-binding residues are conserved in other SETD3 orthologs, suggesting a conserved function of SETD3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The AdoHcy-binding mode of SETD3 is similar to those observed in LSMT and SETD6.
source: The AdoHcy-binding mode of SETD3 is similar to those observed in some other SET domain structures, such as those of LSMT (Trievel et al., 2002) and SETD6 (Chang et al., 2011) (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and reference to figures.

claim: Among AdoHcy-binding residues, Asn278, His279 and Phe327 are conserved in LSMT and SETD6.
source: Among these AdoHcy-binding residues, Asn278, His279 and Phe327 are conserved in LSMT and SETD6, whereas Glu104 and Arg254 are conserved only in LSMT and not in SETD6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Glu104 and Arg254 are conserved only in LSMT and not in SETD6.
source: Among these AdoHcy-binding residues, Asn278, His279 and Phe327 are conserved in LSMT and SETD6, whereas Glu104 and Arg254 are conserved only in LSMT and not in SETD6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Arg75 is an AdoHcy-binding residue that is found only in SETD3.
source: Arg75 is an AdoHcy-binding residue that is found only in SETD3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, the β-actin peptide lies in a narrow groove formed by SET, iSET and C-SET.
source: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, the β-actin peptide lies in a narrow groove formed by SET, iSET and C-SET, with the unmodified or methylated His73 residue snugly accommodated in a pocket composed of α11 of iSET, β6 and β12 of SET, and α12 of C-SET, and η5 of SET (Figure 1C, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The unmodified or methylated His73 residue is snugly accommodated in a pocket composed of α11 of iSET, β6 and β12 of SET, and α12 of C-SET, and η5 of SET.
source: In both substrate-bound and product-bound structures, the β-actin peptide lies in a narrow groove formed by SET, iSET and C-SET, with the unmodified or methylated His73 residue snugly accommodated in a pocket composed of α11 of iSET, β6 and β12 of SET, and α12 of C-SET, and η5 of SET (Figure 1C, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Despite overall structural similarity between substrate-bound SETD3 and AdoMet–SETD3 binary structure (RMSD of 0.66 Å in Cα positions), the region containing two β-sheets of the SET domain (β4-β10-β9 and β3-β11) adopts a conformational change upon peptide binding.
source: When superimposing our substrate-bound complex structure with the previously determined AdoMet–SETD3 binary structure (PDB id: 3SMT), we found that, despite the overall structural similarity between the two SETD3 structures (with a RMSD of 0.66 Å in Cα positions), the region containing two β-sheets of the SET domain (β4-β10-β9 and β3-β11) adopts a conformational change upon peptide binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to structural comparison.

claim: Peptide binding induces the three loops preceding β4, β9 and β11 to shift toward the peptide by 4.2 Å, 4.4 Å and 6.8 Å, respectively.
source: Specifically, peptide binding induces the three loops preceding β4, β9 and β11 to shift toward the peptide by 4.2 Å, 4.4 Å and 6.8 Å, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claim: In the substrate-bound structure, residues Leu67-Glu83 of the β-actin peptide are visible, with His73 occupying a hydrophobic pocket.
source: In the substrate-bound structure, residues Leu67-Glu83 of the β-actin peptide are visible, with His73 occupying a hydrophobic pocket (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The main chain of His73 forms several hydrogen bonds with SETD3, with its main chain amide, Cα, and main chain carbonyl H-bonded to the main chain carbonyl of Tyr313, the side chain carboxyl of Asn256, and the guanidino of Arg316, respectively.
source: The main chain of His73 forms several hydrogen bonds with SETD3, with its main chain amide, Cα, and main chain carbonyl H-bonded to the main chain carbonyl of Tyr313, the side chain carboxyl of Asn256, and the guanidino of Arg316, respectively (Figure 2A).
